know_your_rights.title: Know Your Rights
know_your_rights.subtitle: Key legal rights in Nepal & India

rights.title: Right to Equality
rights.desc: Every citizen is equal before the law. No discrimination on grounds of religion, race, caste, sex, or place of birth.
rights.articles: Nepal Constitution Art. 18, India Constitution Art. 14

rights.title: Right to Life & Dignity
rights.desc: No person shall be deprived of their right to life or personal liberty except according to procedure established by law.
rights.articles: Nepal Constitution Art. 16, India Constitution Art. 21

rights.title: Right to Free Legal Aid
rights.desc: Every citizen has the right to free legal aid from the state if they cannot afford a lawyer.
rights.articles: Nepal Constitution Art. 20, India Constitution Art. 39A

rights.title: Right Against Exploitation
rights.desc: Forced labor and human trafficking are prohibited. No child shall be employed in hazardous work.
rights.articles: Nepal Constitution Art. 17, India Constitution Art. 23-24

legal_faq.title: Common Legal Questions
legal_faq.subtitle: Quick answers to frequently asked legal questions

questions.q: How do I file a police complaint in Nepal?
questions.a: You can file a First Information Report (FIR) at your local police station. You can also file online through the Nepal Police website. Provide your ID, a written statement, and any evidence.

questions.q: What are my rights if arrested?
questions.a: You have the right to know the reason for arrest, to remain silent, to legal counsel, and to be produced before a magistrate within 24 hours.
In Nepal, property is divided equally among legal heirs per the Muluki Ain. In India, the Indian Succession Act governs inheritance. A will can override default rules.

questions.q: What is the process for divorce?
questions.a: Mutual consent divorce takes 6-18 months. Contested divorce requires grounds (cruelty, desertion, conversion, etc.) and may take years. Mediation is often attempted first.

questions.q: Can I get free legal help?
questions.a: Yes. Both Nepal and India provide free legal aid through legal aid commissions and legal services authorities for those who cannot afford representation.

questions.q: How long does a court case take?
questions.a: Civil cases: 1-5 years. Criminal cases: 2-10+ years depending on severity. Supreme Court cases may take even longer. Pre-litigation mediation can speed resolution.

faq_page.subtitle: How to use ल Kanun — for everyone

items.a: ल Kanun is a free AI-powered legal research tool for Nepal and India. It searches through 6,242+ legal provisions to help you find relevant laws and articles.

items.q: Do I need to create an account?
items.a: No. You can search and browse laws without an account. Create a free account to save bookmarks, take case notes, and track your research.
You can search in English, Nepali (नेपाली), and Hindi (हिन्दी). The interface is available in all three languages.

layman.title: For General Users
layman.desc: Simple guides for everyday legal questions

items.q: How do I find a specific law?
items.a: Type your question in the search bar. For example: 'What are the rules for renting a house?' or 'How to register a business in Nepal?' Results are ranked by relevance.
Yes. Type in Nepali script (नेपाली) and the search will find matching provisions. For example: 'घर भाडामा दिने नियम' or 'तलब र ज्याला'.

items.q: What do the percentage scores mean?
items.a: The score shows how relevant each result is to your query. Higher = more relevant. A score of 80% means strong match.

items.q: How do I save important provisions?
items.a: Create a free account, then click the bookmark icon on any search result to save it to your collection.

items.q: Can I use this on my phone?
items.a: Yes. ल Kanun works on any device with a web browser — phone, tablet, or computer.

expert.title: For Legal Professionals
expert.desc: Advanced features for lawyers and judges

items.q: How do I prepare case research?
items.a: Search for relevant legal provisions, bookmark key articles, then use Case Notes to organize your arguments. Link provisions directly to your notes.

items.q: Can I compare Nepal and India laws?
items.a: Yes. Use the country filter in search or browse to compare how Nepal and India handle the same legal issue. Results show which country each provision is from.

items.q: How do I track my research?
items.a: Your search history is automatically saved (if enabled). Access it from Dashboard → Search History. You can also export your bookmarks.
